1.1: This the word the Lord gave to Hosea, son of Beeri, back when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah was runnin' Judah, and Jeroboam—Joash's son—was king over Israel.
1.2: When God first started speakin' through Hosea, He told him straight up: "Go get you a wife who belong to the streets—and have some kids by her too. This whole land been actin' wild, cheatin' on Me spiritually, turnin' their back on Me like I ain't the One who brought them up."
1.3: So Hosea did what God said—he married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim. She got pregnant and gave him a son.
1.4: Then God told Hosea, "Name that boy Jezreel, 'cause I'm 'bout to make the house of Jehu pay for all that bloodshed that went down in Jezreel. I'm 'bout to shut down the whole kingdom of Israel."
1.5: "On that day, I'ma break Israel's strength right in the Valley of Jezreel."
1.6: Gomer got pregnant again and had a baby girl. God said, "Name her Lo-Ruhamah—'cause I ain't showin' no more mercy to Israel. I'm done with 'em. I'm really finna wipe 'em out."
1.7: "But Judah? I'ma still show them love. I'ma save 'em—not with no army, no bows, swords, or horses—but with My own hand. They gon' know it was Me, the Lord their God."
1.8: After Lo-Ruhamah got weaned, Gomer had another son.
1.9: God said, "Name this one Lo-Ammi—'cause y'all ain't My people no more, and I ain't your God."
1.10: But hold up—it ain't over. Even though they ain't actin' like My people now, one day the children of Israel gon' be uncountable, like sand at the beach. You can't measure that. "In that same place where folks said, 'Y'all ain't God's people,' they gon' turn around and say, 'Y'all are children of the livin' God!'"
1.11: Then Judah and Israel gon' link up again—united. They gon' pick one leader over 'em, and rise up outta that land. And when they do? Oh, it's gon' be a big day—Jezreel's day, but this time in victory.

2.1: Tell your brothers, "Y'all my people," And tell your sisters, "God showin' mercy."
2.2: Call out ya mama—yeah, drag her if you got to. She ain't actin' like my wife, and I ain't gon' act like her husband. Tell her to stop wildin' and put away that ho-ish behavior.
2.3: If she don't, I'ma strip her bare—naked like she just got born, Leave her out here dry and thirsty, like a desert wasteland.
2.4: I ain't gon' feel bad for her kids either, 'Cause they came from all that wild livin'.
2.5: Their mama been out here actin' foul—real reckless. She out here sayin', "I'ma chase the ones who spoil me— They give me bread, water, wool, linen, oil, and my drinks too."
2.6: So I'ma block her path with thorns, Put up a wall so she can't find her way.
2.7: She gon' run after them lovers, But she won't catch 'em. She gon' look, but won't find nothin'. Then she gon' come to her senses like, "Let me go back to my first man—he treated me better than this."
2.8: She ain't even realize it was Me— I'm the one who gave her the grain, the wine, the oil, Multiplied her silver and gold— But she used all that to worship Baal. Smh.
2.9: So now I'ma come take back everything— My grain when it's time to eat, My wine when it's time to drink, My wool and linen that was coverin' her shame.
2.10: I'ma expose her dirt in front of everybody she tryin' to impress, And ain't nobody gon' be able to save her from Me.
2.11: All that laughin', all them celebrations—done. No more holidays, new moons, Sabbaths, or feast days. Cut off.
2.12: I'ma destroy them vines and fig trees she thought her lovers paid for. I'ma let it all go wild, let the animals eat it up.
2.13: She gon' pay for all the days she worshipped them fake gods, Burnin' incense, wearin' jewelry, and chasin' lovers— But forgot about Me," says the Lord.
2.14: "But look, I ain't done with her. I'ma bring her out to the wilderness, Speak gently to her heart.
2.15: I'ma give her back her vineyards, Turn the Valley of Trouble into a doorway of hope. She gon' sing again—like she did back in the day, When I brought her outta Egypt.
2.16: On that day," says the Lord, "You gon' call Me 'Husband,' not just 'Master.'
2.17: I'ma erase the name of them Baals from your mouth— You won't even remember their names no more.
2.18: That day, I'ma make peace with nature for y'all— The animals, the birds, the crawlin' things. I'ma break the bow and sword—no more war. You gon' lay down in safety.
2.19: I'ma marry you forever— In righteousness, justice, love, and mercy.
2.20: I'ma lock it in with faithfulness. And you? You gon' finally know Me for real.
2.21: When that day comes," says the Lord, "I'ma answer the sky, and the sky gon' answer the earth.
2.22: The earth gon' respond with grain, wine, and oil. And they gon' bless Jezreel."
2.23: I'ma plant her in the land for Myself. I'ma show mercy to the one I said I wouldn't. And to the one I said, 'You not mine'? I'ma say, 'You mine now.' And they gon' say, 'You my God.'

3.1: Then the Lord said to me, "Go again—love that woman who still out here messin' around, sleepin' with somebody else. Love her anyway, just like I love Israel, even though they steady runnin' to other gods and crushin' on them pagan snacks—raisin cakes and all."
3.2: So I went and bought her back. Paid fifteen silver coins and a lil' over a bushel of barley to get her.
3.3: And I told her, "You stay right here with me. No more wildin', no more jumpin' from man to man. You gon' be mine, and I'ma be yours. We locked in."
3.4: 'Cause Israel? They gon' be without a king, without leadership, without sacrifices, without their spiritual props—no pillars, no priest garments, none of that.
3.5: But after all that time, they gon' come back. They gon' start lookin' for the Lord again, and for David's kingly line. They gon' finally have that deep respect for the Lord—and realize how good He really is, especially in the end times.

4.1: Listen up, y'all—Israel, hear what the Lord gotta say. He bringin' charges against everybody in the land. Ain't no truth out here, no kindness, Ain't nobody even tryin' to know God.
4.2: Folks out here swearin' falsely, lyin', killin', stealin', Cheatin' left and right— No self-control at all. It's just blood on top of blood.
4.3: That's why the land hurtin'. Everybody in it wastin' away— Even the animals in the field, the birds in the sky, Shoot, even the fish in the sea disappearin'.
4.4: Don't nobody try to check nobody else, 'Cause y'all just like the folks who argue with the priest— Like, who you tryna school?
4.5: That's why y'all gon' fall flat in broad daylight, And even the so-called prophets gon' stumble in the dark. God said, "I'ma take your mama out too."
4.6: My people bein' destroyed 'cause they don't know nothin'. Y'all rejected knowledge, so I'ma reject you from reppin' Me as priests. Y'all forgot about My law? Bet—I'ma forget your kids too.
4.7: The more y'all multiplied, The more y'all sinned against Me. So I'ma turn your "shine" into shame.
4.8: They out here eatin' off the sins of the people, Cravin' evil like it's a full-course meal.
4.9: What the people do, the priests do too. So I'ma check both of 'em—punish 'em for how they livin', Pay 'em back for all they done.
4.10: They gon' eat but never be full. They gon' cheat but never grow or thrive. Why? 'Cause they stopped listenin' to Me.
4.11: Adultery, wine, and that strong drink got they hearts in a chokehold.
4.12: My people out here askin' wooden statues for advice, Lookin' to a stick for answers. That cheatin' spirit got them all twisted, They done turned they back on God.
4.13: They makin' sacrifices on mountaintops, Burnin' incense under shady trees—oaks, poplars, and terebinths— Just 'cause the spot feel nice. That's why their daughters out here actin' wild, And their new brides out here steppin' out.
4.14: I ain't even gon' punish the daughters or the brides, 'Cause the men doin' the same thing— Hittin' up temple prostitutes and offerin' sacrifices with 'em. A people with no understanding? Gon' get stomped out.
4.15: Israel, if you gon' act triflin', fine— But Judah? Don't follow behind them. Don't go to Gilgal, don't head to Beth Aven, And don't be swearing fake oaths like, "As the Lord lives" when y'all ain't livin' right.
4.16: Israel stubborn as a hard-headed calf. God gon' let them wander off like a lonely lamb in the wild.
4.17: Ephraim done locked in with idols. Leave him be.
4.18: They drunk on rebellion, Caught up in cheatin' nonstop. The leaders? They love mess. They love what's dirty.
4.19: Now the wind done swept them up, And they gon' be put to shame because of all them fake sacrifices.

5.1: Listen up, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! And you too, king's crew—better open your ears. This judgment right here? It's for y'all. Y'all been setting traps in Mizpah, Spreading nets over Tabor like y'all huntin' people.
5.2: These rebels? Deep in the mess—killin' and wildin'. But I'm checkin' every last one of 'em.
5.3: I know Ephraim like the back of My hand, And Israel? You can't hide from Me. Ephraim out here cheatin', And Israel? Y'all dirty now.
5.4: They don't even try to come back to Me. That cheatin' spirit got a hold on 'em, And they don't really know who I am.
5.5: Israel too proud—and it shows. So both Israel and Ephraim gon' trip over they own sin. And guess what? Judah fallin' right with 'em.
5.6: They gon' show up with all they sheep and cattle, Tryna seek Me like it's business as usual. But I'm gone. I done dipped on 'em.
5.7: They played Me foul, Raised up kids that don't even know Me. Now this New Moon festival they love so much? It's gon' swallow them and everything they got.
5.8: Blow the ram's horn in Gibeah! Sound the trumpet in Ramah! Shout out loud at Beth Aven— "Benjamin, you better look over your shoulder!"
5.9: Ephraim gon' be laid out on judgment day. And I'ma make sure every tribe in Israel know—I meant what I said.
5.10: Judah's leaders movin' boundary lines like crooks. So I'ma pour My anger on 'em like floodwaters.
5.11: Ephraim gettin' crushed—judged hard— Why? 'Cause he chose to follow man's rules over God's.
5.12: So now, I'ma be like a moth to Ephraim—eatin' away slow, And like rot in Judah's bones—decay from the inside.
5.13: Ephraim saw he was sick. Judah felt the pain too. But instead of comin' to Me, They ran to Assyria, tried to holler at King Jareb. But he ain't got the cure. He can't fix this wound.
5.14: I'ma be like a lion to Ephraim, And like a young lion to Judah. I'ma snatch 'em up, tear 'em down, and dip— Ain't nobody comin' to rescue.
5.15: I'ma go back to My place and wait, 'Til they finally admit what they did wrong. Then they gon' come lookin' for Me, Hurtin' and desperate, cryin' out for real.

6.1: Come on, y'all—let's get back to the Lord. Yeah, He cut us, but He the same One who can heal. He hit us hard, but He also the One who can patch us up.
6.2: After two days, He gon' revive us. On the third day? He gon' raise us up, So we can live right in front of Him again.
6.3: Let's get to know Him—really know Him. Let's chase after that knowledge of the Lord. He steady like the sunrise, And He gon' come to us like rain— That spring rain, that fall rain, all of it. Just right.
6.4: "Ephraim, what I'm supposed to do with you? And you too, Judah? Y'all love don't last. It's like fog in the morning— There for a second, then gone. Like dew that disappears.
6.5: That's why I had to cut y'all down with the prophets, Slice y'all up with My words. My judgment hit like lightning in the sky.
6.6: I don't want no empty sacrifices— I want mercy. I want y'all to know Me, Not just burn stuff on an altar.
6.7: But just like Adam, they broke the covenant. Right there, they acted shady toward Me.
6.8: Gilead? Full of evil— Bloodstains everywhere.
6.9: And the priests? They ain't no better. They roll like gangs, waitin' to ambush folks on the road to Shechem. Straight-up scandalous.
6.10: I done seen some wild stuff in Israel's house. Ephraim out here wildin' in spiritual adultery. Israel stay unclean.
6.11: And Judah? Don't think you off the hook. You got a harvest comin' too— When I bring My people back home from captivity."

7.1: Every time I tried to heal Israel, Boom—Ephraim's dirt came out. Samaria's wickedness got exposed. They out here scamming folks, Thieves creepin' in the house, And gangs robbin' folks outside.
7.2: They don't even think in they hearts, "Yo, God see all this mess." But I do. Their own actions surround them like a trap— They right in My face.
7.3: They got kings smilin' over their evil, And princes laughin' at all their lies.
7.4: They all out here cheatin'—every last one. Burnin' hot like an oven. Like a baker who don't touch the fire after kneading the dough, Just lettin' it rise, lettin' it build up.
7.5: On the king's day, The princes got him turnt up off wine, Actin' a fool with the rest of the clowns.
7.6: Their hearts stay preheated like an oven— Schemin' in silence. The baker sleepin' at night, But come morning, the fire blowin' up like flames.
7.7: All of them burnin' up with heat, Takin' out their own judges. All their kings keep fallin', And still—nobody callin' on Me.
7.8: Ephraim out here blendin' in with everybody else— He like a pancake that never got flipped—burnt on one side, raw on the other.
7.9: Outsiders been drainin' his strength, But he too clueless to even notice. He got gray hairs poppin' up all over, But he still actin' brand new, like he ain't see it.
7.10: Israel's pride standin' right there on his face, But still won't come back to Me. Won't even look My way.
7.11: Ephraim act like a silly dove—no common sense at all. One minute he cryin' out to Egypt, Next thing he runnin' to Assyria.
7.12: But wherever he fly, I'ma throw My net over him— Bring him down like a bird fallin' from the sky. I'ma check him real good, Just like I warned y'all in church.
7.13: Woe to them—they ran away from Me! Destruction comin' 'cause they broke My trust. I saved them, but they still out here lyin' on Me.
7.14: They cryin' on they beds at night, But it ain't real. They ain't talkin' to Me with their hearts. They just gatherin' up food and drink, Still tryna rebel.
7.15: I'm the one who trained them, gave them strength, But all they do is plot evil against Me.
7.16: They try to come back, But it ain't to Me—it ain't to the Most High. They like a busted bow that can't even shoot straight. Their leaders gon' die by the sword 'Cause of all the foul things they been sayin'. And Egypt? Gon' clown them hard for it.

8.1: Blow that trumpet loud! The enemy comin' like an eagle swoopin' down on God's house— Why? 'Cause they broke My covenant And straight-up rebelled against My law.
8.2: Israel gon' cry out, "God! We know You!" But they ain't actin' like it.
8.3: They rejected what's good, So now the enemy right behind 'em, ready to pounce.
8.4: They picked kings without askin' Me. They made princes I ain't even co-sign. Then they took their silver and gold, Built up their own idols— And that's what's gon' destroy them.
8.5: That golden calf in Samaria? Nope. Rejected. God mad for real. How long y'all gon' keep actin' like y'all innocent?
8.6: That idol came from Israel— A man made that thing. It ain't God. That fake calf in Samaria? It's gettin' smashed to pieces.
8.7: They out here plantin' wind, But they gon' harvest a whole tornado. Ain't no crops comin' from their foolishness. And even if somethin' did grow, Foreigners gon' eat it all up.
8.8: Israel done got swallowed whole— Now they out here livin' among the nations Like some raggedy bowl nobody wanna use.
8.9: They ran off to Assyria, Actin' like a wild donkey out here by itself. Ephraim out here buyin' love—hiring nations like escorts.
8.10: But even though they out here payin' other nations, I'ma gather 'em back Myself. And they gon' feel that sorrow, 'Cause now they gotta answer to kings who ain't playin'.
8.11: Ephraim built too many altars for sin, And now they just stuck sinning more and more.
8.12: I wrote My laws clear as day, Big blessings, real guidance— But they looked at it like it was foreign, like it ain't even apply to them.
8.13: They bringin' Me sacrifices, Burnin' the meat and eatin' it like I'm impressed— But I ain't acceptin' none of it. Now I'ma remember all their wrongs, And I'ma punish 'em. They gon' end up back in Egypt.
8.14: Israel forgot who made 'em. They out here buildin' fake temples, And Judah? Stackin' up fortified cities. But I'ma send fire on all they cities— Them palaces? Burnt down. Period.

9.1: Don't be out here celebratin', Israel— Not like the other nations. You been out here cheatin' on God, Lovin' up on every threshin' floor like you for sale.
9.2: But guess what? That threshin' floor and winepress ain't gon' feed you no more. That new wine? She dried up.
9.3: Y'all ain't stayin' in God's land. Ephraim goin' back to Egypt, And they gon' end up eatin' unclean food in Assyria.
9.4: Don't even think about offerin' no wine to God— He ain't acceptin' none of that. Y'all sacrifices? Trash. They like funeral bread—makes anybody who touch it unclean. That bread just for your own survival, It ain't comin' into God's house.
9.5: So what y'all gon' do on God's feast day? On that special day He set aside?
9.6: Y'all already scattered 'cause the land destroyed. Egypt gon' scoop y'all up, Memphis gon' handle the burials. Nettles gon' take over your silver, Thorns takin' up space in your tents.
9.7: The time for payback is here—punishment time. Israel see it now. The prophet look crazy, The spiritual man sound insane— All 'cause your sin too heavy and your hate run deep.
9.8: Ephraim's watchman used to roll with God, But now even the prophet got traps set— Foulness done made its way into the temple too.
9.9: These folks are straight corrupt, Like back in the days of Gibeah. God ain't forgot none of it— And He gon' punish every bit.
9.10: God said: "I found y'all like grapes in the wild—rare and sweet. Y'all ancestors were like early figs—first harvest goodness. But then y'all ran off to Baal Peor, Linked up with that mess, And turned into what you worshipped—pure filth.
9.11: Ephraim's glory gone like a bird that flew off— No babies, no pregnancy, no nothin'.
9.12: And even if they do raise kids, I'ma snatch 'em away till none left. It's gon' be ugly when I walk away from 'em."
9.13: Ephraim used to be like Tyre—planted nice, lookin' blessed. But now? They bringin' their kids straight to the killers.
9.14: Lord, give 'em what they askin' for… What should You give? Give 'em wombs that miscarry, Breasts that don't feed.
9.15: Everything wrong with them started in Gilgal— That's where I started hatin' on their behavior. 'Cause of all that evil, I'ma kick them out My house. Ain't lovin' them no more. Their leaders? Straight rebellious.
9.16: Ephraim already hit—root dried up. They can't grow no fruit. And even if they somehow have kids, I'ma take the ones they hold dearest.
9.17: My God gon' throw them out, 'Cause they ain't listen. They gon' end up wanderin' all over the world, Lost among the nations.

10.1: Israel been actin' like a vine that only feeds itself. The more fruit they had, the more altars they built— The more they prospered, the more they dressed up them fake worship spots.
10.2: But their heart divided—two-faced. Now they guilty for real. God gon' smash their altars And tear down them sacred pillars.
10.3: Now they sittin' around sayin', "We ain't got no king— Guess we ain't fear the Lord. And even if we had a king, What he really gon' do for us?"
10.4: All they do is run they mouths, Make fake promises, break covenants. That's why judgment spreadin' like poison plants Growin' in the fields.
10.5: Samaria scared over that golden calf at Beth Aven. The people mournin' for it, The priests screamin' over their idol— 'Cause its glory is gone.
10.6: That same idol? Shipped off to Assyria as a little gift to King Jareb. Ephraim gon' feel deep shame, And Israel? Embarrassed over their own dumb decisions.
10.7: Samaria's king? Cut off like a twig floatin' downstream—powerless.
10.8: Them high places in Aven, where they sinned? Gone. Destroyed. Thorns and weeds takin' over the altars. And the people gon' be cryin' out, "Mountains, fall on us! Hills, cover us!"
10.9: "Israel, y'all been messin' up since Gibeah— And y'all never changed. That fight in Gibeah didn't fix nothin'. Still out here actin' lawless.
10.10: But when I'm ready? I'ma check 'em Myself. I'ma call the nations against 'em— And tie them up for all they double-sins."
10.11: Ephraim used to be like a trained cow Lovin' to stomp out the grain—real comfortable. But I put a yoke on that pretty neck. Ephraim gon' pull the plow now. Judah? You plow too. Jacob? Time to break up that hard ground.
10.12: Sow righteousness—plant what's right. You'll harvest mercy. Break up that hard heart—it's time to seek the Lord, 'Til He show up and rain down righteousness.
10.13: But y'all? Y'all been plantin' wickedness, So all you reap is sin. You eatin' the fruit of lies 'Cause you trusted your own game plan And thought your army was enough.
10.14: That's why chaos about to break out in your streets. All your strongholds? About to get raided like when Shalman tore up Beth Arbel— Mamas and babies caught up in the violence.
10.15: That's what's comin' for you, Bethel, 'Cause y'all been straight evil. At sunrise? Israel's king gon' be completely wiped out.

11.1: When Israel was just a kid, I loved him. I called My son outta Egypt—brought him out with My own hand.
11.2: But the more I called 'em, The more they ran off. They sacrificed to them Baals, Burned incense to carved-up idols.
11.3: I'm the one who taught Ephraim how to walk, Held them up by the arms—steadyin' them. But they ain't even realize it was Me who healed 'em.
11.4: I led them with kindness, Pulled them close with cords of love. I took the yoke off their neck like a good master. I even bent down and fed 'em.
11.5: They not goin' back to Egypt, But Assyria gon' rule over 'em— Why? 'Cause they hard-headed and refuse to turn around.
11.6: The sword comin' to they cities, Gon' cut down their neighborhoods, Gon' eat up everything— All 'cause they listenin' to bad advice.
11.7: My people stuck in reverse, Always backslidin'. They call My name, sure— But they don't lift Me up. Not really.
11.8: Ephraim… how can I let you go? Israel… how can I hand you over? You want Me to treat you like Admah? Like Zeboiim? Man, My heart hurt just thinkin' about it— My compassion kickin' in heavy.
11.9: I ain't gon' go off in rage like that. I ain't gon' wipe y'all out. 'Cause I'm God—not man. I'm the Holy One right here among y'all, And I ain't showin' up to terrify.
11.10: They gon' follow after Me again. I'ma roar like a lion— And when I do, My kids gon' come runnin' back, Tremblin' from the west.
11.11: They gon' return shaky like birds from Egypt, Like doves flyin' in from Assyria. And I'ma let 'em come home again," Says the Lord.
11.12: Ephraim been circlin' Me with lies, Israel been slick with the deceit. But Judah still walkin' with Me— Still rollin' with the Holy One who keep it real.

12.1: Ephraim out here chasin' the wind— Runnin' after that east wind like it's gon' fill him up. Every day he addin' more lies, more destruction. He makin' shady deals with Assyria, And shippin' oil off to Egypt.
12.2: And the Lord got smoke with Judah too. God gon' check Jacob for how he been movin', Gon' pay him back for all the dirt he done.
12.3: Jacob grabbed his brother's heel in the womb— And when he got older, he wrestled with God.
12.4: Yep, he struggled with the Angel—and came out on top. He cried, begged for mercy. He found God at Bethel, And that's where God spoke to us.
12.5: That same God is the Lord of Heaven's Armies— That's the name that still got weight.
12.6: So you? With God's help, turn back. Do right—show mercy, walk in justice. And keep waitin' on God like your life depend on it.
12.7: Ephraim actin' like a slick Canaanite— Keepin' dirty scales in his hands, Lovin' to cheat and oppress folks.
12.8: He out here sayin', "I'm rich now. Got wealth on my own. Ain't nobody gon' find sin on me, I'm good." (But he delusional.)
12.9: But God like, "I'm the same Lord who brought you outta Egypt. And I'ma make you live in tents again— Just like y'all did during the feasts, back in the day."
12.10: "I been speakin' through My prophets, Givin' y'all visions on visions, Breakin' things down through symbols and stories."
12.11: But Gilead still full of idols— Empty nonsense. They still sacrificin' bulls in Gilgal, But them altars? Gon' be turned into piles of rubble in the fields.
12.12: Remember Jacob? He ran off to Syria, Worked just to get a wife— Tended sheep just to marry her.
12.13: Same way, it was through a prophet That the Lord brought Israel outta Egypt, And kept 'em safe through the prophet's word.
12.14: But Ephraim made God mad—real mad. So now God gon' leave his bloodguilt on him, And return all that shame right back to his doorstep.

13.1: Ephraim used to speak with fear and respect—he was that dude in Israel. But once he started worshippin' Baal? That's when his downfall started.
13.2: And now? The sin don't stop. They makin' silver statues, craftin' idols by hand, Showin' off their skills—but it's all fake. They even tell folks, "Go ahead, kiss them calf idols if you worshippin'!"
13.3: But they gon' vanish like morning clouds, Disappear like early dew. They gon' blow away like husks off the threshin' floor, Or drift like smoke out a chimney. Gone.
13.4: "But I been your God since Egypt. You ain't supposed to know nobody else but Me. Ain't no other Savior but Me."
13.5: "I was there for you in the wilderness, When everything around you was dry and dead."
13.6: "But soon as you got comfortable, Full from the pasture I gave you, You got cocky. And then? You forgot about Me."
13.7: "So now I'ma come at you like a lion, Layin' low like a leopard in the cut."
13.8: "I'ma attack like a bear that lost her babies— Rip your chest wide open. I'ma eat y'all like a lion, And let wild animals finish what's left."
13.9: "Israel, you brought this on yourself. You destroyed. But I'm still the only One who can help you."
13.10: "I'm your real King. Where them other ones at? Them fake kings y'all begged for—can they save your cities? Where them judges y'all trusted?"
13.11: "I gave you a king when I was mad, And took him away when My anger hit."
13.12: "Ephraim's sin been stored up—like a tab that's past due. And I ain't forgot."
13.13: "He gon' feel pain like a woman in labor. But he so foolish, He won't even come out the womb when it's time— Like he don't know when to be born."
13.14: "But I'ma still redeem them from death. I'ma pull 'em back from the grave. Death, I'm comin' for you like a disease. Grave, I'm 'bout to shut you down. But don't expect no pity—none."
13.15: "Ephraim might be fruitful now, But the east wind—My wind—is comin' from the desert. It's gon' dry up his spring, Kill his fountain, And wipe out all his treasures."
13.16: Samaria? Guilty. She rebelled hard against her God. Now they gon' die by the sword. Babies gon' be dashed, And pregnant women gon' be ripped open.

14.1: Israel, come on back to the Lord your God. You trippin' and fallin' 'cause of your own mess.
14.2: Bring some real words with you—don't come empty. Say this when you come back to Him: "God, please take away all this sin. Show us grace. We bringin' you our praise instead of burnt offerings."
14.3: "Assyria can't save us. We not ridin' in on war horses. And we done callin' these man-made things 'gods.' Only You, Lord, show mercy to the ones with no father."
14.4: God say, "I'ma heal them from all that backslidin'. I'ma love them real and free— 'Cause My anger ain't on them no more."
14.5: "I'ma be like dew to Israel— Fresh, soft, and life-givin'. He gon' grow like a lily, And plant his roots deep like the trees in Lebanon."
14.6: "His branches gon' stretch wide, Lookin' strong and beautiful like an olive tree. His presence gon' smell sweet—like Lebanon in bloom."
14.7: "People gon' chill in his shade, Come back and find life again— Like grain risin' up, Like vines growin' strong. And the whole place gon' smell like fine wine."
14.8: Ephraim gon' say, "Man, what I need idols for now?" God say, "I been listenin'. I been watchin'. I'm like a green tree that stay fresh year-round— If you see fruit in your life, know it came from Me."
14.9: Who really wise out here? Let 'em get this. Who got sense? Pay attention. 'Cause the Lord's ways are right— If you righteous, you walkin' in 'em. But if you stay tryna cut corners? You gon' keep trippin over what's real.
